findings.desc: Test coverage does not load-bear the authority_job_create provider CLI schema change. The implementation changed command-catalog provider from z.enum([codex, claude-code, gemini]) to z.string().min(1), but the added tests only call submitAuthorityJobFromPlan directly with custom provider strings and inspect signed envelopes. No command catalog or CLI surface smoke asserts that authority_job_create.provider is string/min(1) or invokes the command with a custom provider, so a regression back to the enum would still let the direct submitter tests pass while the actual CLI/tool argument boundary rejects custom provider declarations.
findings.resolvedReason: Added command-catalog-smoke schema assertions that authority_job_create.provider accepts host-neutral custom declarations codex-cli and antigravity, which would fail under z.enum([codex, claude-code, gemini]). Verified with npm --prefix packages/main run build and node packages/main/dist/tasks/command-catalog-smoke.js.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/authority-client.ts:1546-1550 only rejects provider === fake after calling normalizeAuthorityRunnerProvider. That normalizer lowercases only known aliases/canonical codex/gemini but preserves unknown raw values (authority-mode.ts:420-426), and the command schema now accepts any non-empty provider string (command-catalog.ts:2227). As a result, authority_job_create --provider Fake or FAKE is treated as a custom non-fake declaration and can be signed/submitted even though the job-create path promises a non-fake provider declaration. Fix by rejecting the reserved fake provider case-insensitively (for example, check raw.trim().toLowerCase().replace(/_/g, -) === fake) before preserving custom provider spelling.
findings.resolvedReason: Added case-insensitive reserved fake rejection before preserving custom provider spelling in authority_job_create server provider normalization. Added authority-client-smoke coverage for fake/Fake/FAKE rejection plus codex-cli spelling preservation. Verified with npm --prefix packages/main run build and node packages/main/dist/tasks/authority-client-smoke.js.

findings.desc: serverProviderFromPlan treats an explicit reserved fake provider override the same as no override. normalizeServerProvider("fake") returns null, then serverProviderFromPlan falls through to jobPlan.providerPolicy.primaryProvider, so a real-provider JobPlan plus authority_job_create --provider fake can still sign and POST a real provider job. This silently turns an explicit test-only provider declaration into a live Authority job instead of failing closed. Fix by distinguishing override presence from normalization result: if override is present and invalid/fake, return an error; only fall back to JobPlan primaryProvider when no override was supplied.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed serverProviderFromPlan so supplied invalid/fake overrides fail closed instead of falling back to JobPlan primaryProvider. Added smoke coverage for codex-primary JobPlan with fake/Fake/FAKE/empty overrides rejecting without POST and absent override still falling back. Verification passed: npm --prefix packages/main run build; node packages/main/dist/tasks/authority-client-smoke.js; node packages/main/dist/tasks/command-catalog-smoke.js.
